test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 09 Dec 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed only on the grounds of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**proven misbehaviour or incapacity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **judge of the Supreme Court **can be** removed only on the grounds of proven misbehaviour or incapacity**.
 
• An **order of the President must be passed** after an address in **each House of Parliament,** **supported by a majority of the members present and voting and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of those present and voting, and presented to the President in the same Session** for such removal on the ground of such proven misbehavior or incapacity.
 
• Otherwise, a judge of the Supreme Court cannot be removed from office. The **practice of law in any court **or before any other body in India** is prohibited for anyone who has served as a judge of the Supreme Court.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ​The **process for removal judges is outlined in Article 124(4)** of the Indian Constitution. The **President must issue an order** before removing a **Supreme Court Judge** from office.
 
• The **consent of both Houses of Parliament is required** for such an order. It needs a particular majority of the members who are present and voting within the same session.
 
• The **criteria for **removal a**re proven misconduct or incompetence**. After giving notice to the **Speaker or Chairman of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha**, respectively, it comes to light.
 
• A **three-judge panel conducts a thorough examination**. They **present the report during the following joint session** of both Houses of Parliament.
